title: Mouse Without Borders Portable 1.0.1-rc.14
summary: Sharper drag previews with clean transparent edges, up to three file-type icons, and right-click cancellation across PCs.
changes: Use larger Windows file-type artwork and per-pixel transparency to remove the magenta cutout and avoid enlarging small icons.
Show up to three distinct selection types, including a folder icon when folders are selected, plus the total item count. Same-type selections use a small repeated-icon stack.
Right-click during a cross-PC drag cancels it on both PCs, clears the preview and suppresses the context menu and following drop. Delayed cancellation cannot dismiss a different offer.
Keep RC13 transfer progress, queue arrows, recovery, settings and installation behavior.
testing: Install RC14 on BOTH PCs. Drag one file, several files of one type, and a mixture of folders and file types. Check the type icons and total count.
Check previews over light and dark backgrounds and at your Windows display scaling. Move between monitors; the preview should follow the cursor without taking keyboard focus.
While holding a cross-PC drag, right-click, then release the buttons. The preview should disappear on both PCs, no context menu should open and no copying should start.
Immediately try another drag and complete it. Also test cancelling while moving between PCs. Ordinary right-click outside a cross-PC drag should still open menus.
Recheck mouse/keyboard sharing, clipboard, completed transfers, disconnect/reconnect and sleep/wake.
known_limitations: Use the same RC on both PCs for folder/type previews and coordinated cancellation. Older senders provide names only, so folders cannot always be identified.

Icons come from the receiving PC’s installed file associations, not file contents or thumbnails. Windows may only provide small artwork for some types; those icons remain small rather than being blurred by enlargement.
The count is the number of selected top-level files and folders, not every file inside selected folders.
Automated Windows checks do not replace real two-PC testing. Full-speed transfers can still cause lag on busy Wi-Fi.
